beats.caption: Two Stewards sit down to build The Quiet Vale together.

pause.title: Two Stewards, one settlement
pause.text: The Quiet Vale is co-operative: the Vanguard and the Knight build one settlement and share one Warehouse, which starts with 10 of each resource. Twelve rounds make three Seasons. Each turn a Steward has four actions. This game’s Quest Card is The Workings: complete either half for +20 Renown. The demo plays on by itself and stops when something is worth a closer look.

options.label: Vanguard
lines: Once a Season, a Travel tile for no action
Objective: tiles on both sides of the river, joined by a Bridge (+15)

options.label: Knight
lines: Once a Season, a Housing tile for no action

beats.caption: Vanguard secretly seeds three cards into the Encounter Deck.

pause.title: Seeding the Season
pause.text: Before Round 1, each Steward secretly slips three cards from their hand into the Encounter Deck: one near the top, one in the middle, one near the bottom. Vanguard puts the Arrival where it will come out first, while the Warehouse is full, and pushes the Burden as late as possible. Knight does the same with No Soul Goes Unserved, Help Stands and River Breaks Its Banks.

options.label: Top: Blade to Herb
lines: An Arrival, seen early and paid while resources are plentiful

options.label: Middle: First Harvest Bounty
lines: A Boon, more useful once there is something to boost

options.label: Bottom: Houses, Not Homes
lines: A Burden, kept back until the settlement can absorb it

options.label: Not on top: Houses, Not Homes
lines: It would strike in Round 1, before anything is built

beats.caption: Knight secretly seeds three cards into the Encounter Deck.
Round 1: Season I begins. Revealed: No Soul Goes Unserved (arrival) and Blade to Herb (arrival).
Vanguard builds a Lumber Yard, free.

pause.title: The first action
pause.text: Round 1 revealed No Soul Goes Unserved and Blade to Herb. Arrivals wait beside the board for 3 rounds: pay their cost to welcome them and unlock a Special tile, or they leave, costing 10 points and a Strain. With time on the clock, Vanguard starts with production. A Lumber Yard scores nothing by itself, but it is free and refills the shared Warehouse every time it is activated. Tiles that score at once cost resources the Warehouse will need for those Arrivals.

options.label: Use the Season power for a Common Land

Vanguard builds a Common Land for 2 Metal and 2 Herbs.
Vanguard ends the turn. Knight’s turn.
Knight builds a Common Land for 2 Metal and 2 Herbs.

Round 2. Revealed: Pickaxe Reveals Passage (boon) and Omen of Discontent (burden).
Vanguard resolves Omen of Discontent for 2 Herbs. It is set aside for good.

pause.title: Set the Burden down now?
pause.text: Omen of Discontent stays on the table after it strikes. Left alone it costs 10 points at the end and strikes again each time a Season begins, and the price to resolve it rises with the Seasons. In Season I it is cheap, so Vanguard spends an action on it now.

options.label: Resolve it for 2 Herbs
lines: +10 at the end, compared with leaving it

options.label: Leave it and build
lines: −10 at the end, and it strikes again next Season

beats.caption: Vanguard welcomes No Soul Goes Unserved for 2 Herbs and 2 Goods, unlocking Alms House.

pause.title: Welcome them now?
pause.text: No Soul Goes Unserved has 2 timers left, and the Warehouse can pay today. Waiting saves nothing: the cost never falls, and the Special tile it unlocks starts scoring as soon as it is built. Alms House: “When placed or activated: Up to 2 adjacent tiles gain Supported.” Blade to Herb is waiting too, so clearing this one now leaves room for the next.

options.label: Welcome them for 2 Herbs and 2 Goods

Round 5: Season II begins. Revealed: Hearthbound Circle (arrival) and Dark Decay to Light (arrival).

pause.title: Season II begins
pause.text: Each Steward seeded three more cards. No Burden was left on the table to strike again: setting them down early has paid off. From now on Burdens use their Season II text, which is harsher. Hearthbound Circle and Dark Decay to Light are waiting, and the Warehouse holds 11 Wood, 8 Stone, 2 Metal, 3 Food, 12 Herbs and 4 Goods.

pause.title: Linked production
pause.text: Matching production tiles that touch form a Linked group. The first time a group is activated in a round, every tile in it produces, for one action: here two Gathering Outposts make 4 Herbs. Later activations that round produce from one tile only.

pause.title: Houses, Not Homes strikes
pause.text: “Choose 2 Housing Tiles. Each: pay 1 Food or 1 Goods, or +1 Strain.” Paying 2 Food or Goods would keep the tiles clean, but the Warehouse is down to 0 Food and 0 Goods. So the Strain lands. Each Strain costs 10 at the end, and a tile with 3 is Overstrained: it stops working and scores nothing.

pause.title: Season III begins

From now on Burdens use their Season III text, which is harsher. Songs of War to Ore is waiting, and the Warehouse holds 6 Wood, 8 Stone, 2 Metal, 0 Food, 10 Herbs and 0 Goods.

pause.text: Burdens now cost three times their Season I price to resolve. With the game nearly over, they will not get another Season to strike, but each one still costs 10 points at the end. Vanguard has the resources for both, and no other action this late adds 10 points.

pause.title: Nothing left worth doing
pause.text: In the last round, resources left in the Warehouse score nothing, so only actions that add points matter. Vanguard has two actions left and none of them would raise the score. Arrivals still waiting when the game ends do not count against the settlement.

The twelfth round ends, and with it the game.

pause.title: A settlement of 30 tiles
pause.text: Every Arrival was welcomed in time (Battle to Cattle came out in the last round), both Steward objectives were met, and the Quest Card’s easier half, The Mine Road, was completed. What held the score back came late: 7 Strain left on the tiles and Houses, Not Homes and The Quiet Fractures still on the table, −90 in all. Season III Burdens strike hard, and a Warehouse with no Food or Goods cannot pay them off. Twelve rounds, one settlement: that is The Quiet Vale.
